Chief at COP31 health day ministerial Credit: Kiara Worth | UN Climate Change The inclusion of Dynamic and Resilient Health Systems in the COP31 Presidency’s ten priority themes signals growing recognition that health is both a frontline impact of climate change and a foundation for effective climate response. Resilient health systems help countries anticipate, prevent and respond to climate-related health risks while advancing equity, continuity of care and long-term social resilience. The dedicated COP31 Health Day took place on the first day of the Conference, today, coinciding with the thematic priorities on Food and Agriculture. Speaking at the Health Day Ministerial Roundtable Meeting, UN Climate Change Executive Secretary Simon Stiell said health belongs at the heart of climate action. “We need country-led programmes to build resilient health facilities, powered by clean power and enough clean water, protected by better surveillance and early warnings, with workers trained for the risks that are already here,” said Stiell. The World Meteorological Organization released its State of the Climate Update 2026 at COP31 this afternoon, with details of climate indicators like temperatures, ocean heat and sea level, and extreme weather. It shows impacts on health and food security, especially in light of the record El Niño. The report was launched at a press conference with WMO Secretary-General Celeste Saulo, UN Climate Change Executive Secretary Simon Stiell and Wellcome’s Director of Climate and Health Alan Dangour. It will be the 31st session of the United Nations Climate Change Conference , part of the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC). Planning [ edit ] Murat Kurum , Turkey's Minister of Environment, Urbanization and Climate Change , will be the chair of COP31. Chris Bowen , Australia's Minister for Climate Change and Energy , will preside over negotiations. Australia and Turkey had both made bids to host COP31. United Nations rules require a global consensus on a host country; if no agreement had been reached, it would have automatically been hosted in Bonn as the headquarters of the agency that oversees the Paris Agreement . [ 2 ] [ 3 ] Australia's Albanese government had prioritised hosting the conference, which it planned to host in Adelaide , and campaigned for its bid over three years. [ 3 ] Representatives of both countries negotiated during COP30 as neither would withdraw their bid, although neither Recep Tayyip Erdoğan nor Anthony Albanese attended. [ 4 ] After a week of negotiations in November 2025, Turkey and Australia compromised by allowing Turkey to host, while Australian Minister for Climate Change and Energy Chris Bowen will preside over negotiations. [ 2 ] [ 3 ] Organisation and key people [ edit ] In advance of COP31 in Antalya, there was a pre-COP meeting in Fiji from 5–8 October including a leaders' event in Tuvalu to enable world leaders "to see Pacific climate destruction" in advance. [ 5 ] [ 6 ] During COP31, heads of states will attend a World Leaders' Summit in Antalya on November 11 and 12. The summit will take place on day three and four for the conference, in contrast to summits at previous COPs held on the first two days or immediately prior to the COP. [ 7 ] Murat Kurum , the Turkish Minister of Environment, Urbanization and Climate Change will serve as the COP President. [ 8 ] Halil Hasar, the Head of Climate Change at that Ministry and first lady Emine Erdoğan may be prominent. [ 9 ] Minister for Climate Change and Energy for Australia Chris Bowen will be Vice-President and President of Negotiations. [ 8 ] [ 10 ] Although Australia chairs the formal negotiations Turkey is responsible for the Action Agenda. [ 11 ] Turkey's Chief Climate Negotiator is Fatma Varank . [ 12 ] Samed Ağırbaş, President of the Zero Waste Foundation, will serve as Climate High-Level Champion for COP31. [ 13 ] Working alongside the High-Level Champion for COP30, Ağırbaş' role focuses on mobilizing ambitious climate action from businesses, financial institutions, cities, regions, civil society and communities to support governments in achieving the goals of the Paris Agreement. [ 14 ] Non-government participation [ edit ] Greenpeace said that coal subsidies in Turkey are a waste of money, greenhouse gas emissions by Turkey should be reduced, and called for a just transition to stop burning coal , strong adaptation policies and civil society participation. [ 15 ] Academic İbrahim Özdemir has called for universities, civil society organizations, and climate activists to be given a "meeting and contribution platform". To tackle the root cause, countries must phase out fossil fuels – fast and fairly. Secretary-General's Call to Action on Extreme Heat Crippling heat is everywhere. Billions of people around the world are wilting under increasingly severe heatwaves driven largely by a fossil-fuel charged, human-induced climate crisis. More than 70 per cent of the global workforce – 2.4 billion people – are now at high risk of extreme heat. The most vulnerable communities are hit hardest. In response to the rapid rise in the scale, intensity, frequency and duration of extreme heat, UN Secretary-General António Guterres has called for an urgent and concerted effort to enhance international cooperation to address extreme heat. In the face of scorching heat domes and raging wildfires, the Secretary-General renewed his appeal in July 2026 for action in four areas: Protect people before heat becomes deadlier. Make work safer. Build and retrofit for the heat that is coming. Stop fueling the crisis. Secretary-General's remarks Strengthening Global Action The UN Secretary-General's Call to Action on Extreme Heat brings together the diverse expertise and perspectives of ten specialized UN entities (FAO, ILO, OCHA, UNDRR, UNEP, UNESCO, UN-Habitat, UNICEF, WHO, WMO) in a first-of-its-kind joint product, underscoring the multi-sectoral impacts of extreme heat. In support of the Call to Action, the Global Heat Health Information Network launched a set of Heat Action profiles, mapping heat-related work across 16 UN and international organizations. Call to Action HEAT ACTION PROFILES Every city and country should have heat-health action plans, early warning systems and public health measures that reach every community in time. Topics Adaptation and resilience Workstreams Global goal on adaptation Overview Decisions and conclusions Workshops & Events Reports and publications Article 7 of the 2015 Paris Agreement established the global goal on adaptation, which aims to enhance adaptive capacity, strengthen resilience, and reduce vulnerability to climate change, with a view to contributing to sustainable development and ensuring an adequate adaptation response in the context of the temperature goal referred to in Article 2. The UAE Framework for Global Climate Resilience Following a two-year process, the Glasgow–Sharm el-Sheikh work programme, at CMA 5 (2023) Parties adopted the UAE Framework for Global Climate Resilience under, as part of the UAE Consensus . The framework includes a range of thematic and dimensional targets for climate adaptation and resilience. Belém Adaptation Indicators CMA 5 also established the two-year UAE–Belém work programme on indicators for measuring progress towards the targets outlined in the framework. Following an expert-led process, at CMA 7 (2025) Parties adopted a set of 59 Belém Adaptation Indicators , reporting on which will serve as an input to the global stocktake. Belém–Addis Vision on Adaptation CMA 7 also established the Belém–Addis Vision on Adaptation, comprising a two-year policy alignment process that will progress alongside further technical work on metadata and methodologies for the indicators, undertaken by the Subsidiary Bodies. The Baku Adaptation Roadmap At CMA 6 (2024), Parties launched the Baku Adaptation Roadmap (BAR) with the aim of advancing progress in line with Article 7, paragraph 1, of the Paris Agreement. CMA 7 decided that two workshops per year will be held under the BAR and requested the secretariat to prepare a technical paper. The topics of these workshops are informed by submissions from Parties. CMA 6 also established the Baku High-Level Dialogue, an annual event held in the margins of CMA sessions and co-organized by the current and outgoing COP Presidencies. 9(a) Water and sanitation Significantly reducing climate-induced water scarcity and enhancing climate resilience to water-related hazards towards a climate-resilient water supply, climate-resilient sanitation and access to safe and affordable potable water for all 9a(a) Level of water stre
